name: Mauritanian Thieboudienne
description: Thiéboudienne, fish and rice cooked in a tomato-vegetable sauce, is beloved across Mauritania as it is throughout the wider Senegambian coastal region.
steps_detailed: Brown the fish briefly, 3-4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Simmer the tomatoes and 2 cups water 10 minutes.
Add the carrot and cabbage, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Return the fish to warm through before serving.

name: Mauritanian Mechoui
description: Méchoui, whole roasted lamb, is a genuine Mauritanian celebration dish reflecting the country's nomadic pastoral heritage, made here as a smaller roasted cut.
steps_detailed: Rub the lamb with the garlic and cumin.
Roast at 375F (190C) for 25-28 minutes until cooked through and well browned outside.

name: Mauritanian Couscous
description: Couscous, tiny steamed semolina granules, is a beloved Mauritanian staple, shared with the wider Maghreb and reflecting real Berber culinary roots.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, and cumin in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Pour the boiling broth over the dry couscous, cover, and let steam 5 minutes, then fluff.
Serve the stew and broth over the couscous.
